cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T3's test week; T11 answers T10's waiting claim directly.
cells.limitation: T5 pivots to adaptation without answering T4's novelty objection.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 introduces motive readings absent from openings; T8 turns them into forks.
cells.limitation: T5's 'adaptation cuts both ways' is asserted but its second side never developed.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Money versus hours (T1-T2) and forecast versus test (T3-T4) are examined.
cells.limitation: No turn weighs commute expenses or the new job's content against the raise.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 reshapes the test idea into negotiation after T4's objection; T11 qualifies T10.
cells.limitation: T2's unequal-hours critique is never folded into the Life-Accountant's ledger.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D reframes the question as what the raise is for.
cells.limitation: T1's raise-per-hour question is left uncomputed, even as a rough ratio.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T5 gives the strongest case for the raise: money that clears debt.
cells.limitation: T7 says it contests T6's readings but never engages either one.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 names the novelty flaw in a test week; T9 narrows in answer.
cells.limitation: T2's 'all hours as equal' objection gets no answer from the Life-Accountant.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1's Walden line and T2's commuting finding match the sources as recalled.
cells.limitation: T5's commute-adaptation claim sits under a Kahneman basis; suspected loose attribution.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T4 flags 'my own extension of Thoreau'; T6 labels readings as readings.
cells.limitation: T7's 'no commute is a good price' states a conditional too absolutely.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T11 grants waiting is serious, then names staying as a prediction too.
cells.limitation: T9 narrows its claim without citing T4's novelty argument as the cause.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A and T5 ask what the raise would actually change.
cells.limitation: Whether the new work itself appeals is never asked as part of the concern.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 converts 90 minutes each way into three daily hours.
cells.limitation: The 25% and roughly 15 weekly hours are never set against each other.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section D asks what the user pictures the money doing or protecting.
cells.limitation: T10's shop-price limit reflects the speaker's frugality more than stated user priorities.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: Section A lists unknowns: pay, hours, flexibility, travel mode.
cells.limitation: Section A says the commute 'adds' 90 minutes, assuming no current commute.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T8 forks security, escape and worth, each with an implied step.
cells.limitation: Current commute is never asked; current pay listed without what each answer implies.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T6 and T7 offer security, escape and worth as alternatives; D asks.
cells.limitation: T7's 'buying approval by the hour' edges toward a verdict on one motive.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T11 exposes that staying is also a prediction; T2 exposes equal hours.
cells.limitation: The assumption that the 25% is net gain after commute costs goes unexamined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section D contrasts what the money would do with what declining protects.
cells.limitation: Time with family or health appears only as T4's passing 'missed dinner'.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T6 names fear of falling behind; T7 names others' verdict on worth.
cells.limitation: Fear of regret over declining the offer is not raised.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D: 'Only you can say whether any of the readings' resembles you.
cells.limitation: T7 pre-decides the worth branch for the user before T8's fork.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Take, wait (T10), negotiate (T9), trial runs (T3), closer job (T8).
cells.limitation: Accepting while continuing to search nearer is not considered.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T11: staying carries risk too; neither choice is free.
cells.limitation: Commute fares or fuel, which shrink the raise, and negotiation risk are never costed.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: raise closes debt and remote days possible favours taking.
cells.limitation: T8's 'how much money is enough' gets no threshold; T9's two remote days ungrounded.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E names pay, hours, flexibility and months-long feel as decisive.
cells.limitation: Current commute length, which sets the real added time, is omitted.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Ask for flexible terms, rush-hour trial runs, write a limit first.
cells.limitation: No step to compute the net raise after commute expenses.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1's 'part-time job you work for free' makes the cost plain.
cells.limitation: T2's 'Both errors push the same way' compresses two findings tersely.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T6 'That question' maps to T5; T9 'my own claim' maps to T3.
cells.limitation: T7 signposts 'contest both' yet only adds a third reading.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns, all within 25 to 65 words; sections short.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Thoreau's shop and tourist idiom stands apart from the other two.
cells.limitation: Happiness Auditor and Experimenter share one measured register across T2-T11.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Section E condenses T8's forks into conditions rather than repeating turns.
cells.limitation: Section E repeats T9-T10's steps almost as stated.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T4's 'month eight has dark mornings and a missed dinner'.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay generic; few turns besides T4 make the daily cost concrete.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T7's third reading, the 25% as others' verdict, surprises plausibly.
cells.limitation: T9's narrowing names no earlier argument as its cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: Thoreau in T4 and T10 sounds wry and stubborn.
cells.limitation: Experimenter's voice in T3, T6, T9 is flat and interchangeable.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T7: 'buying approval by the hour'; T4: 'a tourist's view'.
cells.limitation: T2 and T11 lines are sound but unremarkable.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T6-T8 build from motive readings to a fork with momentum.
cells.limitation: Turn lengths and intensity stay level from T1 to T11.

strengths: T6-T8 offer security, escape and worth as alternative motives, then fork the advice by each.
T11 answers T10's costless-waiting claim by naming staying as a prediction too.
Section E states observable conditions, debt gap and employer flexibility, with the option each favours.
weaknesses: No mind raises commute fares or fuel, which directly shrink the 25% raise (T1-T11).
T1's raise-per-hour question is never computed, and Section A assumes no current commute.
Experimenter's T9 narrowing names no cause; its voice and the Auditor's sound alike.

symptoms.observed: No turn weighs commute fares or fuel against the raise.
symptoms.evidence: So what is the raise per hour of life, really?

symptoms.observed: Section A assumes zero current commute; the baseline is never asked.
symptoms.evidence: it adds 90 minutes of commuting each way

symptoms.observed: Per-hour ratio posed but never roughly computed; enough-money threshold left open.
symptoms.evidence: compute how much money is enough

symptoms.observed: Narrowing of the test claim cites no earlier argument as cause.
symptoms.evidence: I will narrow my own claim. Testing helps, but

symptoms.observed: Announces contesting T6's readings, then adds a third without engaging them.
symptoms.evidence: I will contest both. A third reading fits

findings.description: The claim that people adapt to commutes less than expected comes from commuting research outside Kahneman's book; attribution under that basis is loose.
The summary says the job adds 90 minutes each way; the user stated the commute would be 90 minutes, not the increase over a current commute.
The Walden quotation and the commuting-unpleasantness finding match recall but cannot be checked against sources here.

rubric_fit_notes: The user supplied only two facts, so personal-relevance cells rest mainly on how the debate handled missing information; ratings there reflect that thin input rather than invented context.
question_type_note: Read as a decision question; every cell applied as written.
